name: Disitamab vedotin
summary: Disitamab vedotin (RC48) is a HER2-directed ADC with an MMAE payload. It was licensed from RemeGen in 2021 by Seagen, now Pfizer, for every market outside RemeGen's Asian territory, with tiered high-single-digit to mid-teens royalties. The pivotal trial is SGNDV-001 (NCT05911295, 412 patients, primary completion 2027-01-29): DV with pembrolizumab against platinum chemotherapy in untreated HER2-expressing (IHC 1+ or higher) la/mUC. In RemeGen's Chinese analogue, RC48-C016 (NEJM), DV with toripalimab doubled median PFS to 13.1 months from 6.5. The price anchor is Padcev, the 1L la/mUC incumbent, at its CMS Part B figure of $109,818 per beneficiary. Uptake is anchored on EV+P's measured 51% of US 1L starts in 2024, halved as a judgement for a follower regimen restricted to HER2. Pfizer booked a $1.6bn impairment on DV in 2025 on updated long-range forecasts.

therapy_mode.source: NCT05911295: DV plus pembrolizumab given in cycles until progression or unacceptable toxicity, against a fixed course of platinum chemotherapy
therapy_mode.note: Oncology treated to progression is chronic by house convention.

list_price_per_patient.source: python3 /tmp/claude-0/price/lookup.py demand Padcev: Part B 2024, $641,224,462 over 5,839 beneficiaries = $109,818 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: House convention: Padcev (enfortumab vedotin) is the closest marketed comparator. It is an MMAE ADC, and with pembrolizumab it is the 1L la/mUC standard DV+P would compete against. Case against: CMS per-beneficiary spend is a part-year figure. Padcev's 2024 Part B units (18,152,640 of 0.25 mg over 5,839 beneficiaries) are about 777 mg a beneficiary, roughly four 21-day cycles, so a full treated year costs several times this. The house 0.5 gross-to-net is calibrated to offset exactly that part-year basis (backend/gross_to_net.py), so the figure is used as the convention intends. No published annual list price for DV exists, since it is not approved in the US.

gross_to_net_pct.source: House convention on a CMS per-beneficiary price (backend/gross_to_net.py: halving lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net prices). The AZD5335 seed carries the same value (lookup.py seed AZD5335).
gross_to_net_pct.note: Net is 50% of list. Direction checked: this is the share OFF list. Case against: Part B spending is paid at ASP plus 6%, which already sits near net, so for a buy-and-bill ADC the true rebate is smaller than 50%. The convention's halving compensates for the part-year price above rather than measuring a rebate.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: RC48-C016, NEJM 2025 (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2511648; https://www.nejm.org/doi/abs/10.1056/NEJMoa2511648): median PFS 13.1 months with DV plus toripalimab against 6.5 with chemotherapy, 484 patients with untreated HER2-expressing la/mUC. 1 - exp(-12/13.1) = 0.600 a year
discontinuation_pct.note: Derived with the brief's accepted exponential conversion from median PFS. SGNDV-001 has not read out, so the closest pivotal is RemeGen's same-design Chinese trial, with toripalimab rather than pembrolizumab. Case against: median time on treatment usually falls short of PFS, which would mean faster discontinuation, and the population and PD-1 partner differ from SGNDV-001.

forecast_start_year.source: NCT05911295: primary completion 2027-01-29, active and not recruiting (ctx trials list). Dual primary endpoints PFS and OS (Future Oncology 2025, doi:10.1080/14796694.2025.2535280).
forecast_start_year.note: JUDGEMENT on timing. An event-driven readout in H1 2027 and a BLA in 2027 under an 8-month priority review gives approval around H1 2028, so 2029 is the first full year. Case for 2028: an early readout and a fast review. Case for later: the OS dual primary may need more follow-up.

exus_multiple.source: Pfizer FY2025 10-K (0000078003-26-000026), product revenue table held in the book's asset_revenue_regions: Ibrance US $2,710mm, international $1,412mm; 1412/2710 = 0.521
exus_multiple.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator. Padcev's own split ($1,902mm US, $38mm international) cannot be used, because Astellas books Padcev outside the Americas. Ibrance is Pfizer's largest solid-tumour product that Pfizer sells itself worldwide. Case against: Ibrance's international figure includes China and other Asian markets, which fall in RemeGen's territory for DV, so this overstates DV's ex-US reach. Lorbrena (international $616mm against US $407mm) shows how much the ratio varies by product.

economics_share.source: Seagen FY2021 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1060736/000106073622000016/sgen-20211231.htm) and 8-K of September 2021: $200mm upfront for exclusive rights outside RemeGen's territory (Asia excluding Japan and Singapore). RemeGen is 'entitled to a tiered, high single digit to mid-teen percentage royalty based on net sales of disitamab vedotin in Seagen's territory', plus up to $195mm of development and $2.2bn of regulatory and commercial milestones. Pfizer's FY2025 10-K (0000078003-26-000026) still describes DV as 'being developed in collaboration with RemeGen Co., Ltd.'
economics_share.note: JUDGEMENT: 1 minus a 12% blended royalty, a point inside the filed range of about 8% to 15%. The tiers' breakpoints are not disclosed. At modest sales the royalty sits near the bottom tier (about 0.91 kept), and at the top tier 0.85 is kept. Milestones are not netted. Case for 1.0: Pfizer books all sales in its territory and the royalty is a cost of sales, not a revenue split. The field is used here as the share of revenue Pfizer keeps.

prevalence.source: SEER Cancer Stat Facts: Bladder Cancer, estimated new US cases for the year, the figure data/epidemiology.csv carries for 'Urinary Bladder Neoplasms' (84,530)
prevalence.note: Oncology convention: the pool is the year's diagnoses (prevalence = incidence), so the engine uses no carryover. lookup.py pool returns no row for 'Carcinoma, Transitional Cell'. The book's only related figure is 'Urinary Bladder Neoplasms', and this uses that same incidence, so no second figure is introduced for bladder cancer. Case against: urothelial carcinoma includes upper-tract tumours, which are not in the bladder count, so the pool is slightly understated.

incidence.source: As prevalence: SEER bladder cancer new cases, as held in data/epidemiology.csv
incidence.note: Set equal to prevalence per the cancer-pool convention the engine reads (backend/forecast.py).

eligible_pct.source: Two filters. (1) la/mUC: 'Epidemiology of Locally Advanced or Metastatic Urothelial Cancer in the US, Europe and Japan', Value in Health 2017 (https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(17)30461-8/fulltext): 3.8 per 100,000, 12,494 US patients a year; 12,494/84,530 = 0.148. (2) HER2 IHC 1+ or higher, the SGNDV-001 entry criterion: IHC 0/1+/2+/3+ of 39.5/23.5/31.9/5.0% in 'Assessment of the expression pattern of HER2 and its correlation with HER2-targeting antibody-drug conjugate therapy in urothelial cancer' (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2667005423000182), so 60.5%. 0.148 x 0.605 = 0.0894, about 7,560 patients a year.
eligible_pct.note: JUDGEMENT on the arithmetic. The la/mUC count dates from an older incidence base than SEER's current 84,530, so the ratio mixes years. The HER2 series is a single-centre cohort, and a systematic review puts IHC 1+ or higher at up to 70% (PMC9635895), which would raise this to 0.103. Every la/mUC patient is counted as a 1L candidate, which overstates the pool because some are too frail for systemic therapy.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of each year's eligible patients starting
penetration_peak_pct.source: Incumbent: enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (Padcev plus Keytruda). Flatiron Health, ASCO GU 2026, 'Real-world use and effectiveness of first-line EV+P in advanced urothelial carcinoma in the US' (https://www.urotoday.com/conference-highlights/asco-gu-2026/asco-gu-2026-bladder-cancer/166997-asco-gu-2026-real-world-use-and-effectiveness-of-first-line-enfortumab-vedotin-with-pembrolizumab-in-patients-with-advanced-urothelial-carcinoma-in-the-us.html): 420 of 821 1L patients (51%) received EV+P in 2024, against 15% in 2023. 0.51 x 0.5 = 0.255
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: half of what the incumbent measurably captured. On an incidence pool this field is the share of each year's eligible starts. SGNDV-001 compares against chemotherapy, not EV+P, and EV+P is already the standard in HER2-expressing patients, so DV must take share from Pfizer's own Padcev rather than from chemotherapy. Case against, lower: no head-to-head against EV+P, and Pfizer impaired DV by $1.6bn in 2025 and $200mm in 2024 on 'updated long-range commercial forecasts' and 'emerging competition' (FY2025 10-K 0000078003-26-000026), which signals modest expectations. Case higher: fewer grade 3 or worse toxicities than chemotherapy and no EV neuropathy or skin toxicity. Second reader: the 51% figure rests on a conference summary.

ramp_steepness.source: lookup.py seed AZD5335: Enhertu's CMS Part B beneficiaries of 864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105 and 8,410 over 2020 to 2024 (lookup.py demand Enhertu confirms them) fitted to k = 1.08 with a midpoint at 2.2 years
ramp_steepness.note: Reused from the book's HER2 ADC launch fit, the closest measured analogue for a HER2 ADC. EV+P's own 1L uptake, 0.4% in 2022, 15% in 2023 and 51% in 2024, is faster, but two points are too few to fit. Case against: a follower in a line with an established ADC standard may ramp more slowly than Enhertu, which opened a new segment.

ramp_midpoint_year.source: Same Enhertu fit as ramp_steepness (lookup.py seed AZD5335)
